- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; reduce forecasted peaks by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Underestimate prices during early periods of strong sentiment (e.g., sentiment > 0.6) — adjust upward by 2–5% if sentiment is rising.
- Lagged forecasts tend to overreact to recent sentiment shifts; delay peak predictions by 1–2 days if sentiment is trending upward.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 3–5% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- Overshoot correction: if forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward pressure of 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment is consistently low (<0.3) over 5+ days, reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid overconfidence in downward trends.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate volatility — cap forecast variance at 1.5x recent 14-day range unless sentiment is bullish.
